page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top centre, page number at top left. Heading "VENARI LICITVM." below the running head. Engraving in the centre. Four lines of italic verse below the engraving. Catchword at the right below the verse.

p.i: Venandi studium licitum mortalibus esse, Hæc præsens docte sculpta tabella monet: Est tamen in rebus modus, & sunt limina fixa, Ultra quos ratio recta salire vetat.

page.notes: The engraving shows a hunting scene: on the left a huntsman with a dog running, in the centre a mounted rider with a spear and a pack of hounds, on the right a bare-bodied figure holding a spear with a dog. Trees, hills and a church spire lie in the background, and a bird or figure is shown in the upper sky. The catchword at the right is set in bold italic; it reads "Venandi" with a trailing mark that may be a stray stroke. Verse line endings are as printed.
